_comment: Which physical board is which, keyed by the ESP32's factory MAC.
The COM port a board appears on is not a property of the board -- it is
assigned by Windows in whatever order things were plugged in, and it moves.
Four boards were identified by hand three times in one session because of
that. The MAC is burned into eFuse, is unique per chip, and is readable in
two seconds from a blank board with no firmware on it at all, which is
exactly the case where the banner cannot help.
So: identify once, record here, never ask again.
'board' is BOARD_NAME as platformio.ini spells it; 'env' is the PlatformIO
environment to flash it with; 'how' records what the identification was
actually based on, because 'someone assumed' and 'the panel was looked at'
are very different levels of confidence and the file should not hide which.

14:c1:9f:d2:3a:5c.note: ESP32-S3, 8MB PSRAM. The only S3 in the set -- chip type alone identifies it.

a4:f0:0f:8e:3b:d0.note: 4-inch ST7796. Different OUI from the two 2.8-inch boards.
a4:f0:0f:8e:3b:d0.how: boot banner, then confirmed on the panel by the owner

8c:94:df:4e:a9:9c.note: 2.8-inch ILI9341. Same OUI as 6e:e8 -- the pair of identical 2.8s.

skip_ports.COM3: Not a board. A component of the laptop itself -- do not open it, do not flash it.
